stemMd: An engineer says, “If the material is brittle, it fractures without much plastic deformation.” Which observation would refute this universal rule?

options.label: A
options.textMd: A brittle material that undergoes substantial plastic deformation before fracturing.

options.label: B
options.textMd: A material whose brittleness is unknown.

options.label: C
options.textMd: A nonbrittle material that deforms substantially.

options.label: D
options.textMd: A brittle material that fractures with little deformation.

options.label: E
options.textMd: A nonbrittle material that fractures with little deformation.

explanationMd: To refute “if P then Q,” find P true and Q false. A brittle material with substantial plastic deformation is exactly that combination. Nonbrittle cases cannot refute a rule restricted to brittle materials.

distractorRationale.c: The rule does not constrain nonbrittle materials.
distractorRationale.d: That supports the rule rather than refuting it.
distractorRationale.e: The rule does not say only brittle materials can do this.
distractorRationale.b: Without knowing the antecedent, this does not establish a counterexample.
